complications.name: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD)
complications.source_text: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a broad term that includes atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and heart failure, two CVDs common among people with diabetes.

complications.name: Heart failure
complications.source_text: CVD also includes heart failure, and diabetes is a risk factor for incident heart failure, which is at least twofold more prevalent in people with diabetes compared with those without diabetes and is a major cause of morbidity and mortality (11).

complications.name: Chronic kidney disease
complications.source_text: There is an increasing appreciation of the common pathophysiology and interrelationship of cardiometabolic risk factors leading to both adverse cardiovascular and adverse kidney outcomes in people with diabetes, including ASCVD, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease (CKD) (17,18).

complications.name: Hypertension
complications.source_text: Hypertension is common among people with type 1 and type 2 diabetes. Hypertension is a major risk factor for ASCVD, heart failure, and microvascular complications.

complications.name: Hyperlipidemia
complications.source_text: Diabetes itself confers independent ASCVD risk, and among people with diabetes, all major cardiovascular risk factors, including hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and obesity, are clustered and common (2).

complications.name: Obesity
complications.source_text: Diabetes itself confers independent ASCVD risk, and among people with diabetes, all major cardiovascular risk factors, including hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and obesity, are clustered and common (2).

complications.name: Microvascular complications
complications.source_text: Hypertension is a major risk factor for ASCVD, heart failure, and microvascular complications.

complications.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis
complications.source_text: Diabetic ketoacidosis and euglycemic ketoacidosis (266).

complications.name: Euglycemic ketoacidosis
complications.source_text: Diabetic ketoacidosis and euglycemic ketoacidosis (266).

complications.name: Stage B heart failure
complications.source_text: Adults with diabetes are at increased risk for the development of asymptomatic cardiac structural or functional abnormalities (stage B heart failure) or symptomatic (stage C) heart failure.

complications.name: Stage C heart failure
complications.source_text: Adults with diabetes are at increased risk for the development of asymptomatic cardiac structural or functional abnormalities (stage B heart failure) or symptomatic (stage C) heart failure.

complications.name: Peripheral artery disease
complications.source_text: ASCVD broadly refers to a history of acute coronary syndrome, myocardial infarction (MI), stable or unstable angina or coronary or other arterial revascularization, stroke, or peripheral artery disease (PAD) including aortic aneurysm and is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in people with diabetes (1).

complications.name: Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) ≥30 mg/g
complications.source_text: For individuals with albuminuria (urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio [UACR] ≥30 mg/g), initial treatment should include an ACE inhibitor or ARB to reduce the risk of progressive kidney disease (24) (Fig. 10.2).

complications.name: Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) ≥300 mg/g
complications.source_text: An ACE inhibitor (ACEi) or angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB) is suggested for the treatment of hypertension in people with coronary artery disease (CAD) or urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 30–299 mg/g creatinine and is strongly recommended for individuals with urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio ≥300 mg/g creatinine.

complications.name: Coronary artery disease
complications.source_text: In people with diabetes and established coronary artery disease, ACE inhibitors or ARBs are recommended first-line therapy for hypertension (65–67).

complications.name: Hyperkalemia
complications.source_text: Adverse events attributed to blood pressure treatment, including hypotension, syncope, bradycardia, hyperkalemia, and elevations in serum creatinine, occurred more frequently in the intensive treatment arm than in the standard therapy arm.

complications.name: Acute kidney injury
complications.source_text: Treatment with ACE inhibitors and ARBs or MRAs can cause AKI and hyperkalemia, while diuretics can cause AKI and either hypokalemia or hyperkalemia (depending on mechanism of action) (77,78).

complications.name: Hypotension
complications.source_text: Adverse events attributed to blood pressure treatment, including hypotension, syncope, bradycardia, hyperkalemia, and elevations in serum creatinine, occurred more frequently in the intensive treatment arm than in the standard therapy arm.

complications.name: Syncope
complications.source_text: Adverse events attributed to blood pressure treatment, including hypotension, syncope, bradycardia, hyperkalemia, and elevations in serum creatinine, occurred more frequently in the intensive treatment arm than in the standard therapy arm.

complications.name: Bradycardia
complications.source_text: Adverse events attributed to blood pressure treatment, including hypotension, syncope, bradycardia, hyperkalemia, and elevations in serum creatinine, occurred more frequently in the intensive treatment arm than in the standard therapy arm.

complications.name: Elevations in serum creatinine
complications.source_text: Adverse events attributed to blood pressure treatment, including hypotension, syncope, bradycardia, hyperkalemia, and elevations in serum creatinine, occurred more frequently in the intensive treatment arm than in the standard therapy arm.

complications.name: Hypokalemia
complications.source_text: Treatment with ACE inhibitors and ARBs or MRAs can cause AKI and hyperkalemia, while diuretics can cause AKI and either hypokalemia or hyperkalemia (depending on mechanism of action) (77,78).

complications.name: Fetal damage
complications.source_text: During pregnancy, treatment with ACE inhibitors, ARBs, direct renin inhibitors, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs), and neprilysin inhibitors are contraindicated, as they may cause fetal damage.

complications.name: New-onset diabetes
complications.source_text: In fact, there was a possible increased risk of ischemic stroke in the AIM-HIGH trial (154) and an increased incidence of new-onset diabetes (absolute excess, 1.3 percentage points; P < 0.001) and disturbances in diabetes management among those with diabetes in the HPS2-THRIVE trial in those on combination therapy (155).

complications.name: Increased risk of incident type 2 diabetes with statin use
complications.source_text: Several studies have reported a modestly increased risk of incident type 2 diabetes with statin use (156,157), which may be limited to those with diabetes risk factors and/or impaired glucose tolerance.

complications.name: Cognitive dysfunction
complications.source_text: The Antithrombotic Trialists’ Collaboration published an individual participant–level meta-analysis (172) of six large trials of aspirin for primary prevention in the general population.

complications.name: Bleeding
complications.source_text: In ARRIVE, with 12,546 individuals over a period of 60 months of follow-up, the primary end point occurred in 4.29% vs. 4.48% of individuals in the aspirin versus placebo groups (HR 0.96 [95% CI 0.81–1.13]; P = 0.60). Gastrointestinal bleeding events (characterized as mild) occurred in 0.97% of individuals in the aspirin group vs. 0.46% in the placebo group (HR 2.11 [95% CI 1.36–3.28]; P = 0.0007).

complications.name: Major bleeding
complications.source_text: In contrast, major bleeding was significantly increased from 3.2 to 4.1% in the aspirin group (rate ratio 1.29; P = 0.003), with most of the excess being gastrointestinal bleeding and other extracranial bleeding.

complications.name: Gastrointestinal bleeding
complications.source_text: In contrast, major bleeding was significantly increased from 3.2 to 4.1% in the aspirin group (rate ratio 1.29; P = 0.003), with most of the excess being gastrointestinal bleeding and other extracranial bleeding.

complications.name: Extracranial bleeding
complications.source_text: In contrast, major bleeding was significantly increased from 3.2 to 4.1% in the aspirin group (rate ratio 1.29; P = 0.003), with most of the excess being gastrointestinal bleeding and other extracranial bleeding.

complications.name: Reye syndrome
complications.source_text: Aspirin use in individuals aged <21 years is generally contraindicated due to the associated risk of Reye syndrome.

complications.name: Ischemic stroke
complications.source_text: In people with diabetes and prior MI (1–3 years before), adding ticagrelor to aspirin significantly reduces the risk of recurrent ischemic events, including cardiovascular and CHD death (188).

complications.name: Recurrent ischemic events
complications.source_text: In people with diabetes and prior MI (1–3 years before), adding ticagrelor to aspirin significantly reduces the risk of recurrent ischemic events, including cardiovascular and CHD death (188).

complications.name: Cardiovascular death
complications.source_text: In people with diabetes and prior MI (1–3 years before), adding ticagrelor to aspirin significantly reduces the risk of recurrent ischemic events, including cardiovascular and CHD death (188).

complications.name: Major bleeding, including intracranial hemorrhage
complications.source_text: However, a higher incidence of major bleeding, including intracranial hemorrhage, was noted with dual antiplatelet therapy.

complications.name: Intracranial hemorrhage
complications.source_text: However, a higher incidence of major bleeding, including intracranial hemorrhage, was noted with dual antiplatelet therapy.

complications.name: Asymptomatic cardiac structural or functional abnormalities
complications.source_text: Adults with diabetes are at increased risk for the development of asymptomatic cardiac structural or functional abnormalities (stage B heart failure) or symptomatic (stage C) heart failure.

complications.name: Symptomatic heart failure
complications.source_text: Adults with diabetes are at increased risk for the development of asymptomatic cardiac structural or functional abnormalities (stage B heart failure) or symptomatic (stage C) heart failure.

complications.name: Asymptomatic peripheral artery disease
complications.source_text: The risk for PAD in people with diabetes is higher than that in people without diabetes (220–222).

complications.name: Claudication
complications.source_text: Notably, classical symptoms of claudication are uncommon, and almost half of people with newly diagnosed PAD were asymptomatic (223).

complications.name: Foot complications
complications.source_text: In asymptomatic individuals with diabetes and age ≥65 years, microvascular disease in any location, or foot complications or any end-organ damage from diabetes, screening for PAD with ankle-brachial index testing is recommended if a PAD diagnosis would change management.

complications.name: End-organ damage from diabetes
complications.source_text: In asymptomatic individuals with diabetes and age ≥65 years, microvascular disease in any location, or foot complications or any end-organ damage from diabetes, screening for PAD with ankle-brachial index testing is recommended if a PAD diagnosis would change management.

complications.name: Left ventricular hypertrophy
complications.source_text: Individuals at high risk for ASCVD include those with end-organ damage such as left ventricular hypertrophy or retinopathy or with multiple CV risk factors (e.g., older age, hypertension, smoking, dyslipidemia, CKD, and obesity).

complications.name: Retinopathy
complications.source_text: Individuals at high risk for ASCVD include those with end-organ damage such as left ventricular hypertrophy or retinopathy or with multiple CV risk factors (e.g., older age, hypertension, smoking, dyslipidemia, CKD, and obesity).

complications.name: Heart failure hospitalization
complications.source_text: In the FIGARO-DKD trial, finerenone reduced the primary outcome of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for heart failure (HR 0.87 [95% CI 0.76–0.98]; P = 0.03) in people with type 2 diabetes and CKD (240).

complications.name: Worsening heart failure
complications.source_text: The DAPA-HF trial specifically evaluated the effects of dapagliflozin 10 mg daily on the primary outcome of a composite of worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death in individuals with New York Heart Association (NYHA) class II, III, or IV heart failure and an ejection fraction of 40% or less (287).

screening_tests.name: Blood pressure measurement
screening_tests.source_text: 10.1 Blood pressure should be measured at every routine clinical visit, or at least every 6 months by a trained individual who should follow the guidelines established for the general population: measurement in the seated position, with feet on the floor and arm supported at heart level, after 5 min of rest.
screening_tests.frequency: every routine clinical visit, or at least every 6 months

screening_tests.name: Home blood pressure self-monitoring
screening_tests.source_text: Home blood pressure self-monitoring and 24-h ambulatory blood pressure monitoring may provide evidence of white coat hypertension, masked hypertension, or other discrepancies between office and true blood pressure (30,31).
screening_tests.indication: To monitor antihypertensive treatment, identify white coat hypertension, masked hypertension, or discrepancies between office and true blood pressure

screening_tests.name: 24-h ambulatory blood pressure monitoring
screening_tests.source_text: Home blood pressure self-monitoring and 24-h ambulatory blood pressure monitoring may provide evidence of white coat hypertension, masked hypertension, or other discrepancies between office and true blood pressure (30,31).
screening_tests.indication: To monitor antihypertensive treatment, identify white coat hypertension, masked hypertension, or discrepancies between office and true blood pressure

screening_tests.name: Lipid profile
screening_tests.source_text: In adults with prediabetes or diabetes not taking statins or other lipid-lowering therapy, it is reasonable to obtain a lipid profile at the time of diagnosis, at an initial medical evaluation, annually thereafter, or more frequently if indicated. E
screening_tests.frequency: at diagnosis, initial medical evaluation, annually thereafter, or more frequently if indicated
screening_tests.indication: Adults with prediabetes or diabetes not taking statins or other lipid-lowering therapy

screening_tests.name: Coronary artery calcium measurement
screening_tests.source_text: In adults with diabetes ≥40 years of age, measurement of coronary artery calcium is also reasonable for cardiovascular risk assessment.
screening_tests.indication: Adults with diabetes ≥40 years of age for cardiovascular risk assessment

screening_tests.name: Natriuretic peptide measurement
screening_tests.source_text: 10.38a Adults with diabetes are at increased risk for the development of asymptomatic cardiac structural or functional abnormalities (stage B heart failure) or symptomatic (stage C) heart failure. Consider screening adults with diabetes by measuring a natriuretic peptide (B-type natriuretic peptide [BNP] or N-terminal pro-BNP [NT-proBNP]) to facilitate prevention of stage C heart failure.
screening_tests.indication: Adults with diabetes to facilitate prevention of stage C heart failure

screening_tests.name: Echocardiography
screening_tests.source_text: 10.38b In asymptomatic individuals with diabetes and abnormal natriuretic peptide levels, echocardiography is recommended to identify stage B heart failure. A
screening_tests.indication: Asymptomatic individuals with diabetes and abnormal natriuretic peptide levels to identify stage B heart failure

screening_tests.name: Ankle-brachial index testing
screening_tests.source_text: 10.39 In asymptomatic individuals with diabetes and age ≥65 years, microvascular disease in any location, or foot complications or any end-organ damage from diabetes, screening for PAD with ankle-brachial index testing is recommended if a PAD diagnosis would change management. B
screening_tests.indication: Asymptomatic individuals with diabetes and age ≥65 years, microvascular disease in any location, or foot complications or any end-organ damage from diabetes, if a PAD diagnosis would change management

screening_tests.name: Resting electrocardiogram (ECG)
screening_tests.source_text: Candidates for advanced or invasive cardiac testing include those with 1) symptoms or signs of cardiac or vascular disease and 2) an abnormal resting electrocardiogram (ECG).
screening_tests.indication: Individuals with symptoms or signs of cardiac or vascular disease

screening_tests.name: Exercise ECG testing
screening_tests.source_text: Exercise ECG testing without or with echocardiography may be used as the initial test.

screening_tests.name: Pharmacologic stress echocardiography
screening_tests.source_text: Pharmacologic stress echocardiography or nuclear imaging should be considered in individuals with diabetes in whom resting ECG abnormalities preclude exercise stress testing (e.g., left bundle branch block or ST-T abnormalities).
screening_tests.indication: Individuals with diabetes and resting ECG abnormalities precluding exercise stress testing

screening_tests.name: Nuclear imaging
screening_tests.source_text: Pharmacologic stress echocardiography or nuclear imaging should be considered in individuals with diabetes in whom resting ECG abnormalities preclude exercise stress testing (e.g., left bundle branch block or ST-T abnormalities).
screening_tests.indication: Individuals with diabetes and resting ECG abnormalities precluding exercise stress testing

therapeutic_agents.name: Metformin
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Metformin may be used for the management of hyperglycemia in people with stable heart failure as long as kidney function remains within the recommended range for use (310).
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Management of hyperglycemia in people with stable heart failure, provided kidney function is within the recommended range

therapeutic_agents.name: Sodium–glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Therefore, in addition to the management of hyperglycemia, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia, treatment with SGLT inhibitors and/or GLP-1 RAs that have demonstrated cardiovascular and kidney benefit is considered a fundamental element of risk reduction and a core pharmacological strategy to improve cardiovascular and kidney outcomes in people with type 2 diabetes (Fig. 10.1).
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Fundamental element of risk reduction and core pharmacological strategy to improve cardiovascular and kidney outcomes in people with type 2 diabetes

therapeutic_agents.name: Glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Therefore, in addition to the management of hyperglycemia, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia, treatment with SGLT inhibitors and/or GLP-1 RAs that have demonstrated cardiovascular and kidney benefit is considered a fundamental element of risk reduction and a core pharmacological strategy to improve cardiovascular and kidney outcomes in people with type 2 diabetes (Fig. 10.1).
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Fundamental element of risk reduction and core pharmacological strategy to improve cardiovascular and kidney outcomes in people with type 2 diabetes

therapeutic_agents.name: ACE inhibitor
therapeutic_agents.source_text: ACE inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) are recommended first-line therapy for hypertension in people with diabetes and albuminuria or coronary artery disease. A
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: First-line therapy for hypertension in people with diabetes and albuminuria or coronary artery disease

therapeutic_agents.name: Angiotensin receptor blocker
therapeutic_agents.source_text: ACE inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) are recommended first-line therapy for hypertension in people with diabetes and albuminuria or coronary artery disease. A
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: First-line therapy for hypertension in people with diabetes and albuminuria or coronary artery disease

therapeutic_agents.name: Calcium channel blocker
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Start two drugs from ACEi or ARB, CCB† or diuretic‡
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Second-line therapy for hypertension when not meeting goal on one agent
